patients.summary: China-born IT specialist who joined in 2019; the practice found chronic hepatitis B in 2020 (tenofovir via GI), and MEN2A surfaced in 2021 with a pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid carcinoma both resected. In late 2023, after stopping tenofovir on his own, he developed hepatitis B associated polyarteritis nodosa, treated with prednisone and azathioprine; last seen January 2025, with an active-disease rheumatology letter in December 2025.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller Daniel Chen, 37, works in IT, wants a primary care home after several years without a regular doctor. Membership and insurance billing explained. Records release faxed to his last primary care office. New patient visit set for 9/10 at 9:00.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body: 11 pages from his previous primary care office, last visit there in 2016. Contents: two brief annual visits, normal vitals, a normal basic metabolic panel and CBC from 2015, tetanus booster 2009. Allergy list there: sulfa drug (anaphylaxis as a child) and latex (skin reaction). No chronic problems or medications listed. Abstracted to chart; originals scanned.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 37 y/o man, here to set up primary care. Feels well. No ongoing symptoms. Has not had a physical in about three years.

PMH: none. PSH: none. Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis). Sulfa reaction was as a young child, throat closing, per his parents; latex gloves give him an itchy rash.
FH: father had thyroid cancer (he is not sure of the type). Mother has type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure.
SH: born in China. Works as an IT specialist, mostly desk work. Single, lives alone. Never smoker. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drugs.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: BP 136/86 (rechecked, same). Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, thyroid not enlarged, no nodules felt. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, no organomegaly. Skin without rashes. No edema.
PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment/plan:
1. Health maintenance: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c. One-time HCV and HIV screens, he agrees. Tdap today (last tetanus 2009 per old records).
2. BP borderline today: recheck at next visit; less salt, keep moving.
3. Flu shot when this season's supply arrives, nurse visit.
Return in a year or as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Daniel, all of your blood work from this week came back normal: kidney and liver tests, blood counts, cholesterol and sugar are fine, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to do. The flu vaccine should be in by early October; the front desk can book you a quick nurse visit.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM given in the left deltoid. Screening questions negative. Latex-free gloves used. Tolerated well, left after 15 minutes.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit (clinic in-person visits limited this month). Patient at home, identity verified.

S: About two months of feeling tired, worse by mid-afternoon. Also a mild dull ache under the right ribs on and off, not related to meals, no nausea or vomiting. No jaundice that he has noticed, urine normal color, stools normal. Sleeping 7 hours. Working from home now. Mood okay. No fever or weight change. Drinks rarely.

O: Comfortable on video, no scleral icterus visible, speaking in full sentences.

A/P: Fatigue with vague RUQ discomfort, nonspecific. Start with labs: CMP, CBC, TSH. Lab is open mornings by appointment. Will call with results. If pain becomes constant or he turns yellow, call the same day.

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called him about the 4/9 labs. ALT 92 and AST 61, mildly up; bilirubin, blood counts, kidney function and TSH normal. Not taking Tylenol, supplements or anything new. Asked about family liver disease: he says his sister was told years ago she carries hepatitis B. He has never been tested himself that he knows of and does not recall being vaccinated. Ordered hep B surface antigen, core antibody and surface antibody; he can go on the 16th. Added sister's hepatitis B to family history.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Hepatitis B
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit to go over serologies. HBsAg positive, total core antibody positive, surface antibody negative, with the mildly raised ALT/AST from 4/9.

Explained what this means: active hepatitis B infection; with his sister a carrier and birth in China, most likely acquired early in life, but we cannot call it chronic until the surface antigen is still positive after 6 months. He is single, no current partner; reviewed how it spreads (blood, sex, shared razors or toothbrushes). Avoid alcohol and extra acetaminophen.

Still tired, RUQ ache unchanged and mild.

Plan: repeat HBsAg and liver tests in October with his physical, and GI referral at that point if it persists. He prefers to wait given the current situation. Call sooner for jaundice, dark urine or worse pain.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
38 y/o here for yearly exam. Still runs low on energy most afternoons, the right-sided ache comes and goes, no change. No jaundice. Working remotely, eating more takeout than he would like.

Meds: none. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).
FH: father thyroid cancer; mother DM2 and HTN; sister hepatitis B carrier.

Exam: BP 148/94 seated, repeat after 5 minutes 146/92. Well. Thyroid without palpable nodule. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender today, liver edge not felt. No edema. Skin clear.
PHQ-2: 1.

A/P:
1. Elevated blood pressure: second time above 140/90 here, now 148/94, and mother has HTN. Diagnosing essential hypertension. Start with lifestyle: salt under 2 g, back to exercise, fewer takeout meals. Bought a home cuff today at my suggestion; log morning and evening readings for two weeks and send them. Recheck in 3 months, and we talk about medicine then if still high.
2. Hepatitis B surface antigen positive in April: repeat today with liver tests.
3. Flu shot today, R deltoid.
4. Routine labs otherwise up to date from last year.

orders.reason: chronic hepatitis B with raised ALT

documents.title: Result call - hepatitis B
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Spoke with patient. HBsAg remains positive six months after the first test, so this is chronic hepatitis B. ALT 84, AST 57, similar to spring; albumin and bilirubin normal. Referred to gastroenterology for viral load, staging and a treatment decision. He agrees. Referral faxed with April and October labs. Home BP log still to come.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology consultation. Date of service 12/28/2020. Reason: chronic hepatitis B, referred by his primary care physician.

Mr. Chen is a 38-year-old man found this spring to be hepatitis B surface antigen positive, and still positive on repeat in October, so about eight months now. He describes being worn out for several months and a mild intermittent ache in the right upper abdomen. No jaundice, pruritus, GI bleeding or confusion. Rare alcohol. No transfusions or injection drug use. Sister is a known carrier.

Medications: none. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: Comfortable, anicteric. Abdomen soft, minimal RUQ tenderness, no hepatosplenomegaly, no ascites. No stigmata of chronic liver disease.

Data: ALT 92 and AST 61 in April, ALT 84 and AST 57 in October. HBsAg positive both times, core antibody positive. HBV DNA drawn today: 46,000 IU/mL.

Impression: chronic hepatitis B with persistently raised transaminases and moderate viremia. Biopsy will help us judge the degree of inflammation before we commit him to long-term antiviral therapy.

Plan: percutaneous liver biopsy, scheduled 1/12. Will see him by video afterward to review.

Thank you for this referral.
Gastroenterology

reports.text: Specimen: liver, percutaneous needle core biopsy (ultrasound guided, right lobe). Gross: two tan cores, 1.6 and 1.4 cm. Microscopic: chronic portal and lobular inflammation, predominantly lymphocytic, with scattered areas of hepatocyte injury. No steatosis. No dysplasia or malignancy. Iron stain negative.
reports.conclusion: Liver, needle biopsy: chronic hepatitis with chronic inflammation and areas of hepatocyte injury, consistent with the clinical history of chronic hepatitis B.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with food

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up (video)
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology follow-up by video, 1/21/2021.

Biopsy from 1/12 shows chronic hepatitis with inflammation and areas of hepatocyte injury. With persistently raised ALT and HBV DNA of 46,000 IU/mL, he meets criteria for treatment.

Plan: start tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg once daily with food, long term. Counseled not to stop it on his own, since stopping can cause a flare. Prior authorization submitted by our office. Recheck HBV DNA and liver tests in about 6 months. Please keep his blood pressure care with you.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).
Gastroenterology

documents.title: Pharmacy - prior authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy called: Vemlidy prior authorization approved for 12 months (GI submitted). Patient picking up today. Added tenofovir alafenamide to med list as prescribed by GI.

events.reason: Blood pressure; spells of headache and sweating

orders.reason: episodic headache, palpitations, sweating with hypertension; family history of MEN2

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Overdue BP recheck (January visit was cancelled; never sent the home log).

Since around the new year he has had spells: a pounding headache, his heart racing, and drenching sweat, lasting 10 to 30 minutes, a few times a week, no clear trigger. Between spells he feels sluggish. A few episodes of vague belly discomfort. Appetite normal. Home cuff readings he remembers: mostly 150s/90s, one at 180-something during a spell. Taking tenofovir daily since late January without trouble.

Asked again about his father's thyroid cancer. He has since asked his family: father was told he has MEN2 and had medullary thyroid cancer removed; a paternal aunt had an adrenal tumor, a pheochromocytoma. Updated family history.

Exam: BP 158/96, HR 96 regular. Not diaphoretic now. Thyroid: no palpable nodule. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. No tremor.

A/P:
1. Hypertension with paroxysmal headache, palpitations and sweating, and a father with MEN2: pheochromocytoma has to be excluded first. Urgent endocrinology referral today; I called their office and they will see him in early April. Holding off on starting a BP medicine so the workup and any alpha blockade are planned by endocrinology; avoid beta-blocker until then.
2. Chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir per GI.
ED precautions reviewed for a spell with chest pain, severe headache or BP over 200.

orders.reason: family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology new consult, seen 4/5/2021, at the request of his primary care physician.

38-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B, on tenofovir since January after GI evaluation in December. For several months, headaches that come with a racing heartbeat and heavy sweating. Feels more sluggish lately and has had a few spells of vague abdominal discomfort. Eats normally. Denies illicit drugs, decongestants or stimulants.

Family history is notable for endocrine surgery on his father's side: father with MEN2 and medullary thyroid cancer, paternal aunt with pheochromocytoma.

Medications: tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: BP 166/94, HR 92. Alert, not flushed. Neck: no goiter or discrete nodule on palpation. Cardiac exam normal, regular rhythm, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. No marfanoid habitus, no mucosal neuromas.

Impression: spells with hypertension in a man whose father has MEN2. Need to exclude pheochromocytoma and medullary thyroid carcinoma.

Plan: BMP with calcium and serum calcitonin today; 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines (collection starts tomorrow morning); adrenal-protocol CT and thyroid ultrasound this week; germline RET testing sent with his consent. No beta-blocker. Will write again with results.
Endocrinology

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Adrenal protocol CT of the abdomen with unenhanced, portal venous and delayed images, with pelvis included. Left adrenal: fullness of the gland. Right adrenal: normal. Liver normal in size and attenuation without focal lesion. Gallbladder, pancreas, spleen and kidneys unremarkable. No hydronephrosis. Normal caliber aorta. No lymphadenopathy. No free fluid. Pelvic organs unremarkable. Lung bases clear.
reports.conclusion: Left adrenal fullness; correlate with biochemical testing. Right adrenal normal. Otherwise unremarkable.

reports.text: Right lobe 4.6 x 1.7 x 1.6 cm. Left lobe 4.4 x 1.5 x 1.5 cm. Isthmus 0.3 cm. In the right lobe there is a 1.4 cm solid hypoechoic nodule. Left lobe without nodules. No abnormal cervical lymph nodes.
reports.conclusion: 1.4 cm solid hypoechoic right thyroid nodule.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up by video, 4/19/2021, results review.

Results: serum calcium 10.6 mg/dL, borderline high. Calcitonin 186 pg/mL, clearly raised. 24-hour urine normetanephrine 1,120 mcg (reference under 900) and metanephrine 430 mcg (reference under 400), mildly elevated. CT: fullness of the left adrenal, right adrenal normal. Thyroid ultrasound: 1.4 cm solid hypoechoic right lobe nodule. Germline testing: pathogenic point mutation in the RET proto-oncogene.

Impression: multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 (2A pattern) with a left pheochromocytoma and a thyroid nodule that, with this calcitonin, is very likely medullary carcinoma.

Plan:
- Doxazosin 4 mg daily starting today for alpha blockade, liberal salt and fluids. Expect some lightheadedness on standing at first.
- Laparoscopic left adrenalectomy first (tentatively 4/29), then total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection once he recovers. Referral to endocrine surgery sent.
- Genetic counseling referral; first-degree relatives should be offered testing.
Will keep you posted.
Endocrinology

documents.title: Genetic Counseling
documents.author: genetic counselor
documents.body:
Genetic counseling session by video, 4/26/2021.

Reviewed his RET result and what it means: the variant causes MEN2 and is passed on in an autosomal dominant way, so each child of a carrier has a one-in-two chance of inheriting it. It explains his father's medullary thyroid cancer and his aunt's pheochromocytoma. Lifelong surveillance after his surgeries will be run by endocrinology.

He has a sister; we recommend she be tested, and gave him a family letter to share. He has no children. Discussed options for future family planning when relevant.

Questions answered. Letter and result copy sent to the patient.
Medical Genetics

reports.text: Specimen: left adrenal gland, laparoscopic adrenalectomy. Gross: adrenal gland with a well-circumscribed tan-red nodule, 2.4 cm in greatest dimension. Microscopic: nested (zellballen) pattern of polygonal cells with granular cytoplasm; chromogranin and synaptophysin positive. Tumor confined to the gland. Margins clear.
reports.conclusion: Left adrenal gland: pheochromocytoma, 2.4 cm, confined to the adrenal gland; margins clear.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 4/29/2021, discharged 5/1/2021.

Procedure: laparoscopic left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma in the setting of MEN2, after 10 days of alpha blockade with doxazosin 4 mg daily.

Course: uncomplicated surgery. Brief intraoperative BP swings on gland handling, controlled. First postoperative night in step-down; no hypotension or hypoglycemia. Tolerated diet on day 1. Pain controlled with acetaminophen and a short course of oxycodone. Port sites clean.
Blood pressure on the ward ran 136-142/86-90 on doxazosin, so doxazosin is continued at discharge for hypertension; primary care to follow.

Discharge medications: doxazosin 4 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis). Latex precautions observed.

Follow-up: surgery clinic in 2 weeks; endocrinology to arrange the thyroid operation. Pathology to follow.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - after adrenalectomy
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 12 days after laparoscopic left adrenalectomy. Pathology: pheochromocytoma 2.4 cm, confined, clear margins. The spells have stopped completely since surgery. Port sites a little sore. Off oxycodone. Some lightheadedness standing up fast in the first week on doxazosin, better now.

Meds: doxazosin 4 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily.

Exam: BP 138/88. Port sites healing, no redness. Heart RRR. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Pheochromocytoma, resected.
2. Hypertension, still above goal after the tumor was removed: continue doxazosin 4 mg as his BP medicine for now, home log, recheck after the thyroid surgery.
3. MEN2: total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection being scheduled for June by endocrine surgery.
4. Chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir, GI following.

events.reason: Total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning on an empty stomach

reports.text: Specimens: (A) thyroid, total thyroidectomy; (B) central compartment (level VI) lymph nodes. Gross: thyroid 32 g; firm white-tan nodule in the right lobe, 1.3 cm. Microscopic: nests and sheets of round to spindled cells with stippled chromatin and amyloid stroma; calcitonin positive, thyroglobulin negative. Background C-cell hyperplasia. Margins negative. Central compartment nodes: all negative for carcinoma. Parathyroid tissue not identified in the specimen.
reports.conclusion: Medullary thyroid carcinoma, right lobe, 1.3 cm; margins negative; central compartment lymph nodes negative.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - General Surgery
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 6/21/2021, discharged 6/22/2021.

Procedure: total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection for a calcitonin-secreting right thyroid nodule in MEN2. Both recurrent laryngeal nerves identified and preserved. Parathyroids identified and left in situ with blood supply.

Course: voice normal. Calcium checks overnight and in the morning normal; no tingling. Drain removed day 1. Incision clean.

Discharge medications: levothyroxine 125 mcg every morning (new), doxazosin 4 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily, acetaminophen as needed.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Follow-up: surgery clinic 2 weeks; endocrinology in 4 to 6 weeks for calcitonin and TSH. Pathology to follow.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology follow-up 7/20/2021, four weeks after total thyroidectomy with central neck dissection.

Pathology: medullary thyroid carcinoma, 1.3 cm, right lobe, margins negative, central nodes negative. Adrenal pathology from April: pheochromocytoma, confined.

Feels well, voice normal, no tingling. No more spells. Taking levothyroxine correctly.

Labs today: calcitonin undetectable (<2 pg/mL). Plasma free metanephrines normal. TSH and free T4 in range on 125 mcg. Calcium normal.

Impression: MEN2A with medullary carcinoma and pheochromocytoma both resected, biochemically clear.
Plan: continue levothyroxine 125 mcg and doxazosin 4 mg per primary care. Yearly calcitonin, plasma metanephrines and TSH; sooner for any recurrent spells.
Endocrinology

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccine, dose 1
documents.author: RN
documents.body: First Pfizer dose 0.3 mL IM left arm. Delayed his series around the two surgeries. Sulfa anaphylaxis history noted (not a vaccine component); observed 30 minutes, no reaction. Dose 2 booked 8/17.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GI follow-up 8/3/2021. On tenofovir alafenamide since January, no missed doses by his account. Had a busy spring: left adrenalectomy for pheochromocytoma and total thyroidectomy for medullary carcinoma as part of a new MEN2 diagnosis. No abdominal complaints now; energy better.

HBV DNA not detected. ALT and AST now normal.

Plan: continue tenofovir indefinitely. Yearly visit with HBV DNA, liver tests and liver ultrasound for cancer surveillance, starting next summer.
Gastroenterology

documents.title: COVID-19 vaccine, dose 2
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second Pfizer dose right deltoid. Arm sore after the first and tired one day, nothing else. Watched 15 min, fine. Card updated.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam, age 39. Big year medically: chronic hep B now on tenofovir (viral load undetectable in August), MEN2 found in April with left pheochromocytoma removed 4/29 and total thyroidectomy for medullary carcinoma 6/21. Endocrinology letter 7/20: calcitonin undetectable, metanephrines normal.

Today: feels the best he has in two years. Home BPs 130s/80s. Neck scar healing well. No palpitations or sweating spells.

Meds: levothyroxine 125 mcg daily, doxazosin 4 mg daily, tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole (anaphylaxis), latex (contact dermatitis).

Exam: BP 134/86. Well. Neck: healed low collar incision. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, port scars fine. Skin clear. No edema.
PHQ-2: 0.

A/P:
1. Hypertension on doxazosin 4 mg: acceptable today, continue.
2. MEN2A s/p adrenalectomy and thyroidectomy: endocrinology surveillance yearly; levothyroxine per endo.
3. Chronic hepatitis B: GI yearly with ultrasound.
4. Prevention: flu shot today. CMP, CBC, lipids. COVID primary series done in August. Booster when eligible.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daniel, your labs from the physical look good. Kidney function, calcium, liver enzymes and blood counts are normal, and your cholesterol is in a healthy range.

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization report
documents.author: MA
documents.body: State registry update: Pfizer COVID-19 booster given 12/11/2021 at a community pharmacy. Entered in immunization history.
